How it works

From usage limit
to reset reminder.

Quota checks run on your machine. Email delivery uses your Resend account.

Reads what Codex reports.

ResetWatch connects to your signed-in local Codex installation and reads its usage windows. It makes no inference requests.

Remembers the alert.

When a window is exhausted, its reset reminder is saved to a local SQLite database. Restart the watcher and pending alerts resume.

Checks before it emails.

At the expected reset, it rechecks your allowance. The email distinguishes an expected time from confirmed availability, including any other exhausted windows.

1

Download and unpack

Windows x64

In PowerShell, open the folder where you downloaded the archive.

PowerShell
Expand-Archive .\resetwatch_0.1.0_windows_amd64.zip -DestinationPath .\resetwatch
cd .\resetwatch
.\resetwatch.exe version

Keep this folder, or move the binary to a directory on your PATH.

2

Connect Codex

Install Codex and run codex login first. Your sign-in stays with Codex. For Windows shell shims, use --codex-bin with the path to the native codex.exe.

Connect account
.\resetwatch.exe connect codex
3

Set up email, then watch

Create a Resend API key ↗ and use a sender on your verified domain. Replace the three example values below.

Email and watcher
$env:RESEND_API_KEY = 'your_resend_api_key'
.\resetwatch.exe notify --email you@example.com --from 'ResetWatch <alerts@yourdomain.com>'
.\resetwatch.exe watch

For a first Resend test, use onboarding@resend.dev as sender and your own Resend account email as recipient. Other recipients require a verified domain.

Leave the watcher running on an awake, online computer. Ctrl + C stops it safely.

Try it without connecting: .\resetwatch.exe demo

Sample output. No email sent.

Notes

Before you rely
on the reminder.

Local uptime, data handling, and supported accounts.

Does my laptop need to stay on?

Yes. ResetWatch is a local process. Keep the watcher running, or use an always-on machine with its own Codex sign-in. There is no hosted scheduler.

What leaves my machine?

Your recipient, sender, and alert content go to Resend. Quota snapshots, settings, and alert history stay in your local state directory. Your API key is read from the environment, not saved to the database.

What does a delivered alert mean?

An accepted Resend receipt, not guaranteed inbox delivery. Retries reuse one message key within bounded time and attempt limits. Old reset reminders are cancelled after 24 hours.

Which accounts work?

A Codex ChatGPT subscription sign-in that exposes quota data is required; API-key-only accounts are unsupported. This release tracks one Codex account per state directory. Same-email workspace switches cannot be reliably distinguished, so verify quota after switching. Claude is not supported yet.
